Subject: Lifeline Health — post-demo notes and SLO targets

Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo today — overview was helpful. Quick recap from our side so we have alignment going into procurement: 

- Primary product: real-time clinical decision assistant for triage (web + mobile).
- Peak traffic expectation: 10–15 inference requests/sec during peak (northbound burst to 30rps for brief windows).
- Latency SLO: p95 tail target ~120ms for short responses (~200 tokens); p99 under 300ms is preferred.
- Throughput/Batching: we understand batching is useful, but many calls are low-token; want guidance on batching without breaking p95.
- Model requirements: prefer a tuned open-weight model (accuracy > 92% on our internal evals). We may run larger quality-critical flows on a 70B variant and smaller prompt flows on 7B/13B for cost.
- Data residency & compliance: HIPAA-covered PHI; must run in a VPC/private deployment inside us-east-1; SOC 2 evidence required for procurement.
- Fallback behavior: need deterministic fallback model for degraded capacity.

Action items on our side: share the internal SLO matrix and sample prompt traces (attached). Procurement will ask for a deployment sketch and ballpark pricing.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_v1.xlsx, slo_matrix.csv

Appreciate if you can capture recommended topology and next steps (ops handoff + security package).

—Rajesh

Rajesh — thanks for the clear write-up and for sending the prompt traces. Short reply to confirm our read and propose concrete next steps. Below is a summary of what we heard + an initial technical sketch and asks from our side.

What we heard (short):
- Target p95 ~120ms (200-token responses), p99 <300ms; bursts to ~30rps for short intervals; sustained 10–15rps.
- HIPAA + VPC requirement; SOC 2 proof required for procurement.
- Mixed-model strategy: heavier 70B for critical flows + smaller models for routine prompts.

Initial topology recommendation (hybrid Private/Dedicated):
- Private control plane in us-east-1 + Dedicated GPU pool in customer VPC (single-tenant compute).
- Autoscale policy: maintain baseline pool sized for 12rps; short-burst autoscaling with warm standby nodes (scale within 60–90s).
- Model routing: primary routing to 13B quantized variant for routine requests; route critical flows to 70B on dedicated instances. Automated fallback: 13B deterministic variant if 70B is unavailable.
- Latency controls: continuous batching capped at 40ms collection window for short responses, KV/prefix cache for frequent prefixes to shave tokens on hot paths.
- Quantization: 70B recommend 4-bit quant (with accuracy check) + latency-optimized kernels; 13B as int8.
- Proactive canary: 10% traffic canary for first two weeks after rollout; automatic rollback on error rate spike or latency regressions.

Security/compliance & procurement:
- We can provide SOC 2 Type II report and SOC 2 attestation summary; our Private package supports KMS integration and audit logs.
- We'll assemble a security evidence packet (A0) for procurement — Soojin will own this deliverable.

Ballpark cost notes (rough):
- Baseline Dedicated + Private control plane (approx): $45k–$65k/mo depending on burst sizing and 70B usage.
- Cost levers: aggressive prefix caching and routing smaller model for 80% of requests reduces unit cost ~3–4x.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
1) We prepare a deploy sketch and rough cost model (Aditya) — delivery by Thu 5/21.
2) Security packet (Soojin) — first draft by Fri 5/22.
3) Mutual action plan update with milestones for pilot (Ops + Procurement) — we will update the attached MAP and share for signature.

Attachments referenced: redwood_deploy_sketch.pdf (will send in next message).

If that aligns, I’ll loop in Solutions Engineering to schedule a topology deep-dive (45–60m) next week.

Best,
